questions.stem: Number of ways to form 5 digit numbers greater than 50000 with the use of digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 such that sum of first and last digit is not more than 8, is equal to
questions.solution:
$\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}\ \underline{d}\ \underline{e}$
$a \ge 5$
$a + e \le 8$
not all $b, c, d, e$ are zero if $a = 5$.
$\Rightarrow$ (i) $a = 5$
$5\ \_\ \_\ \_\ \underline{e} \Rightarrow e \in \{3, 2, 1, 0\}$
$8^{3}\cdot 4 - 1$ ways
$\Rightarrow$ (ii) $a = 6$
$6\ \_\ \_\ \_\ \underline{e} \Rightarrow e \in \{2, 1, 0\}$
$8^{3}\cdot 3$ ways
$\Rightarrow$ (iii) $a = 7$
$7\ \_\ \_\ \_\ \underline{e} \Rightarrow e \in \{1, 0\}$
$\Rightarrow 8^{3}\cdot 2$ ways
$\Rightarrow$ Total ways
$\Rightarrow 8^{3}(2 + 3 + 4) - 1 = 4608 - 1 = 4607$

questions.solution:
$P(4, 4, 3)$
$\frac{x-1}{2} = \frac{y-2}{1} = \frac{z-1}{1} = \lambda$
Any pint of line $R(2\lambda + 1, \lambda + 2, \lambda + 1)$
$\overrightarrow{PR} : (2\lambda - 3)\hat{i} + (\lambda - 2)\hat{j} + (\lambda - 2)\hat{k}$
$\overrightarrow{PR} \cdot \langle 2, 1, 1 \rangle = 0$
$2(2\lambda - 3) + (\lambda - 2) + 2(\lambda - 2) = 0$
$6\lambda = 10$
$\lambda = \frac{5}{3}$
$\therefore R\left(\frac{13}{3}, \frac{11}{3}, \frac{8}{3}\right)$
Now, $Q(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$
$\frac{\alpha + 4}{2} = \frac{13}{3}, \frac{\beta + 4}{2} = \frac{11}{3}, \frac{\gamma + 3}{2} = \frac{8}{3}$
$\alpha = \frac{14}{3}, \beta = \frac{10}{3}, \gamma = \frac{7}{3}$
$\alpha + \beta + \gamma = \frac{14 + 10 + 7}{3} = \frac{31}{3}$

questions.stem: The sum of squares of real roots of the equation: $x^{2} + |2x - 3| - 4 = 0$, is
questions.solution:
$x^{2} + |2x - 3| - 4 = 0$
(i) $2x - 3 \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \ge \frac{3}{2}$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} + 2x - 3 - 4 = 0$
$x^{2} + 2x - 7 = 0 \Rightarrow (x + 1)^{2} = 8$
$\Rightarrow x = \pm 2\sqrt{2} - 1$
$\Rightarrow x = \left(2\sqrt{2} - 1\right)$
as $-2\sqrt{2} - 1 < \frac{3}{2}$
(ii) $x \le \frac{3}{2} \Rightarrow x^{2} - (2x - 3) - 4 = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} - 2x - 1 - 0 = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 1)^{2} = 2$
$\Rightarrow x = \pm 2\sqrt{2} + 1 \Rightarrow x = -2\sqrt{2} + 1$
as $\sqrt{2} + 1 > \frac{3}{2}$
$\Rightarrow$ two roots are $x = -\sqrt{2} + 1, 2\sqrt{2} - 1$
$\Rightarrow$ Sum of squares $= 12 - 6\sqrt{2} = 6\left(2 - \sqrt{2}\right)$

Let $f(x) = \frac{2^{x}}{2^{x} + \sqrt{2}}$, then $\sum_{k=1}^{81} f\left(\frac{k}{82}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$f(x) = \frac{2^{x}}{2^{x} + 2^{1/2}} = \frac{2^{x}}{2^{x} + \sqrt{2}}$
$f(1-x) = \frac{2^{1-x}}{2^{1-x} + 2^{1/2}} = \frac{\frac{2}{2^{x}}}{\frac{2}{2^{x}} + 2^{1/2}} = \frac{2}{2 + \sqrt{2}\,2^{x}}$
$= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2^{x} + \sqrt{2}}$
$\Rightarrow f(x) + f(1-x) = \frac{\sqrt{2} + 2^{x}}{\sqrt{2} + 2^{x}} = 1$
$\Rightarrow \sum_{k=1}^{81} f\left(\frac{k}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{2}{82}\right) + \left(f\left(\frac{3}{82}\right)\right) + \ldots$
$\ldots + f\left(\frac{40}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{41}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{42}{82}\right)$
$+ \ldots + f\left(\frac{79}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{80}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{81}{82}\right)$
$= \left[f\left(\frac{1}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{81}{82}\right)\right] + \left[f\left(\frac{2}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{80}{82}\right)\right] + \ldots$
$+ \left[f\left(\frac{40}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{42}{82}\right) + f\left(\frac{41}{82}\right)\right]$
$= \underbrace{1 + 1 + \ldots + 1}_{40\text{ times}} + f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$
$= 40 + \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2}} = 40 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{81}{2}$

Let $E_{1} : \frac{x^{2}}{9} + \frac{y^{2}}{4} = 1$ be an ellipse and a series of ellipse are drawn that $E_{i+1}$ has same centre, eccentricity as $E_{i}$ and $E_{i+1}$'s major axis is minor axis of $E_{i}$. If $S_{i}$ be the area of $E_{i}$, then $\left(\frac{5}{\pi}\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} S_{i}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $b_{i}$ be minor axis of $E_{i}$
$a_{i}$ be major axis of $E_{i}$
$\Rightarrow e_{i} = 1 - \frac{b_{i}^{2}}{a_{i}^{2}}$
Now, $b_{i+1}$ minor axis of $E_{i+1}$
$A_{i+1}$ major axis of $E_{i+1}$
$\Rightarrow e_{i+1} = 1 - \frac{b_{i+1}^{2}}{a_{i+1}^{2}}$, also $a_{i+1} = b_{i}$ and $e_{i} = e_{i+1}$
$= \frac{b_{i}^{2}}{a_{i}^{2}} = \frac{b_{i+1}^{2}}{(b_{i})^{2}} \Rightarrow b_{i+1} = \frac{b_{i}^{2}}{a_{i}}$
$\Rightarrow$ Area of $E_{i} = S_{i} = \pi a_{i}b_{i}$
$\Rightarrow S_{i+1} = \pi a_{i+1}b_{i+1}$
$= \pi(b_{i})\left(\frac{b_{i}^{2}}{a_{i}}\right)$
$= \pi(b_{i}a_{i})\left(\frac{b_{i}}{a_{i}}\right)^{2}$
$S_{i+1} = S_{i}(1 - e_{i}^{2})$
$\Rightarrow S_{i+1} = S_{i}\left(1 - \left(1 - \frac{4}{9}\right)\right) = S_{i}\cdot\frac{4}{9}$
$\Rightarrow S_{i} = 6\pi, S_{2} = 6\pi\cdot\frac{4}{9}\ S_{3} = 6\pi\cdot\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)^{2}$
$\Rightarrow \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} S_{i} = \left(\frac{6\pi}{1 - \frac{4}{9}}\right) = \frac{54\pi}{5}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{5}{\pi}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} S_{i} = \frac{5}{\pi}\cdot\frac{54\pi}{5} = 54$

If $\alpha$ is the number of points of discontinuity and $\beta$ is the number of points of non-differentiability, then $(\alpha + \beta)$ is equal to (where [.] denote greatest integer function)

questions.stem: If $\alpha = 1 + \sum_{n=1}^{6}(-3)^{n-1}\cdot{}^{12}C_{2n-1}$, then distance of point $\left(12, \sqrt{3}\right)$ from the line $\alpha x - \sqrt{3}y + 100 = 0$ is,
questions.solution:
$\alpha = 1 + \sum_{r=1}^{6}(-3)^{r-1}\cdot{}^{12}C_{2r-1}$
$= 1 + \sum_{r=1}^{6}\left[\left(\sqrt{3}i\right)^{2}\right]^{r-1}\cdot{}^{12}C_{2r-1}$
$= 1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}i}\sum_{r=1}^{6}\left(\sqrt{3}i\right)^{2r-1}\cdot{}^{12}C_{2r-1}$
Let $\sqrt{3}i = x$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}i}\sum_{r=1}^{6}{}^{12}C_{2r-1}\cdot x^{2r-1}$
$\alpha = 1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}i}\left[{}^{12}C_{1}\cdot x^{1} + {}^{12}C_{3}\cdot x^{3} + {}^{12}C_{5}\cdot x^{5} + \ldots + {}^{12}C_{11}\cdot x^{11}\right]$
Let $(1 + x)^{12} = {}^{12}C_{0}\cdot x^{0} + {}^{12}C_{1}\cdot x^{1} + {}^{12}C_{2}\cdot x^{2} + \ldots + {}^{12}C_{12}\cdot x^{12}$
$(1 - x)^{12} = {}^{12}C_{0}\cdot x^{0} - {}^{12}C_{1}\cdot x^{1} + {}^{12}C_{2}\cdot x^{2} - {}^{12}C_{3}\cdot x^{3} \ldots + {}^{12}C_{12}\cdot x^{12}$
$(1 + x)^{12} - (1 - x)^{12} = 2\left({}^{12}C_{1}\cdot x^{1} + {}^{12}C_{3}\cdot x^{3} + \ldots + {}^{12}C_{11}\cdot x^{11}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}i}\left[\frac{(1 + x)^{12} - (1 - x)^{12}}{2}\right]$
$\alpha = 1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}i}\left[\frac{\left(1 + \sqrt{3}i\right)^{12} - \left(1 - \sqrt{3}i\right)^{12}}{2}\right]$
Since, $\omega = \frac{-1}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}i}{2} \Rightarrow -2\omega = 1 - \sqrt{3}i$
$\omega^{2} = \frac{-1}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{3}i}{2} \Rightarrow -2\omega^{2} = 1 + \sqrt{3}i$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}i}\left(\frac{\left(-2\omega^{2}\right)^{12} - (2\omega)^{12}}{2}\right)$
$= 1 + \frac{2^{11}}{\sqrt{3}i}\left(\omega^{24} - \omega^{12}\right)$
$= 1 + \frac{2^{11}}{\sqrt{3}i}(1 - 1) = 1$
$\alpha = 1, \Rightarrow$ perpendicular distance from $\left(12, \sqrt{3}\right)$ is
$\frac{\left|12 - \sqrt{3}\left(\sqrt{3}\right) + 100\right|}{\sqrt{1^{2} + \left(\sqrt{3}\right)^{2}}} = \frac{109}{2}$

$20\sum_{r=1}^{25} T = 20\times\frac{25}{2}[2a + 24d] = 13$
$d = \frac{1}{20\times 25}$
Substitute a and d in (i)

Now $5m\sum_{r=m}^{2m} T_{r} = 5\times 20\left[\sum_{r=20}^{40} T_{r}\right]$
